clue.text: Large bird once confused with seal

indicators.note: confused says the letters of the preceding words are jumbled into a new order

explanation.surface: A birdwatcher once mistook a large bird for a seal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with' joins the two parts of the fodder: BIRDONCE and SEAL are rearranged together.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words describe something of great size or amount; a synonym pair.

clue.text: Almost everything confiscated by officer, it is mine

indicators.note: something confiscated by an officer is taken into his hands, so it goes inside

parts.note: COP is slang for a police officer

indicators.note: almost the whole word, so its final letter is dropped

parts.note: everything means all
taken as written

explanation.surface: A police officer seizes nearly all someone owns, and that person protests it is theirs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mine' reads as a possessive but is the noun: a pit where coal is dug.
explanation.definitionFit: A coal pit is a type of mine, the place coal is extracted from the ground.

clue.text: A little Latin, or second language of old

indicators.note: A little says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Someone learns a little Latin, or perhaps an old second language.
explanation.definitionFit: Old Norse was the tongue of medieval Scandinavians and Vikings, a language of the past.

clue.text: Start knotting giant ties

indicators.note: knotting twists the letters of the following words together into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone begins tying knots in enormous neckties.
explanation.definitionFit: To instigate something is to set it going or bring it about; a verb synonym.

clue.text: Utter brilliance from Bolshoi Ballet, all concluding

indicators.note: all concluding asks for the closing letter of each of the four words

explanation.surface: A critic praises the dazzling performance of the Bolshoi Ballet company.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Utter' looks like an adjective (sheer) but is the verb, to give out a sound.
explanation.definitionFit: To emit a sound or cry is to utter it, sending it out; verb synonyms.

clue.text: Cook in a large African

indicators.note: to cook figures is to doctor them, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: An instruction to cook something in a big pot or quantity.
explanation.definitionFit: Algeria is a country in North Africa, so a native of it is one example of an African.

clue.text: Fruit no crossword setter likes, initially sent over

indicators.note: sent over, in a down clue, means the pieces are flipped and read upwards

parts.note: taken as written
the setter refers to himself as me

indicators.note: initially asks for the opening letter of the word

explanation.surface: A puzzle setter admits there is a fruit they do not like, delivered to them.
explanation.definitionFit: The lemon is a sour yellow citrus fruit, an example of the category.

clue.text: Popular viewpoint, for example

parts.note: IN means fashionable or popular
a stance is a position or point of view

explanation.surface: A popular opinion is offered as an illustration.
explanation.definitionFit: A case cited to illustrate a point is an example; direct synonyms.

clue.text: Breakfast show broadcast?

indicators.note: broadcast means put out over the air, so the word is spoken and heard

parts.note: a serial is a show told in instalments

explanation.surface: A query about a breakfast television programme going out.
explanation.definitionFit: Cornflakes and similar grain dishes are the classic morning meal, so breakfast stands for the food.

clue.text: A river still spectacular

parts.note: R is the map abbreviation for river
still, at rest, means resting

explanation.surface: A river lying calm makes for an impressive sight.
explanation.definitionFit: Something arresting catches and holds the attention, as a striking or stunning thing does.

clue.text: Disease affecting dog hair good in cat hair, perhaps

indicators.note: in says one letter is placed inside the word for the cat's hair

parts.note: a lion is a big cat, and its hair is a mane; perhaps marks the example

explanation.surface: A vet compares coat ailments in dogs and cats.
explanation.walkthrough: The cat is a lion, so its hair is the mane.
explanation.definitionFit: Mites cause this skin condition in dogs and other animals, leaving the coat patchy.

clue.text: Looking back, quote work in verse

indicators.note: looking back means the joined pieces are read from right to left

parts.note: to quote is to cite
OP, short for opus, is a work

explanation.surface: Someone reflects on a quoted passage of a poem.
explanation.definitionFit: Writing set in lines of metre is poetry, so it is poetic in form.

clue.text: Dark-haired beast about to score

indicators.note: about places the first word around the other one

parts.note: a brute is a beast
to net is to score, as in a goal or a profit

explanation.surface: A dark-haired brute is on the point of scoring.
explanation.definitionFit: A brunette is a woman with brown or dark hair, so the adjective sense fits.

clue.text: Painter — very important person inspires one

indicators.note: inspires, literally breathes in, means the first takes the second inside

parts.note: a titan is a giant figure, someone very important
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A painter has a VIP as his muse.
explanation.definitionFit: The Venetian Renaissance master Tiziano Vecellio is known in English by this name; one painter.

clue.text: Business done, upset

definitions.meaning: the total sales a firm makes in a period
as two words, tipped over or overturned

explanation.surface: Something finished in business was overturned.
explanation.definitionFit: A firm's sales figure is its revenue total; to tip something over is to overturn it.

clue.text: Red first

definitions.meaning: the scarlet colour of a churchman's robes

explanation.definitionFit: Cardinal red is a deep scarlet; cardinal also means chief or fundamental.

clue.text: Cleaning product put off man

parts.note: to deter is to put off
a gent is a man

explanation.surface: A cleaning product that discourages a man from buying it.
explanation.definitionFit: Washing liquids and powders are detergents, agents that remove dirt.

clue.text: Game of chance allowed to get in the way

indicators.note: to get in places the allowed word inside the way

parts.note: a route is the way to go
let means allowed

explanation.surface: A gambling game is permitted to block the path.
explanation.definitionFit: A wheel-and-ball casino game where players bet on the number; a gambling game.

clue.text: Inspector very sour for a change

indicators.note: for a change says the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: An inspector who is normally sweet turns grumpy for once.
explanation.definitionFit: A surveyor examines land or buildings and reports on them, an inspecting professional.

clue.text: Revealing study, Tory gutted

parts.note: to scan is to study closely

indicators.note: gutted means the insides are removed, leaving only the outer letters

explanation.surface: A revealing study shows a Conservative left devastated.
explanation.walkthrough: A TORY is a member of Britain's Conservative Party.
explanation.definitionFit: Scanty clothing shows a lot of skin, so it is revealing; adjective synonym.

clue.text: Complex 'neath southern capital city

indicators.note: complex means intricate or tangled, so the letters are reordered

explanation.surface: A building complex lies beneath a southern capital.
explanation.definitionFit: The Greek capital, an example of a capital city.

clue.text: Principally sensational, except when dull

indicators.note: principally points to the first letter of the word

parts.note: unless means except when

explanation.surface: Something is mainly sensational, except when it is boring.
explanation.definitionFit: A dull, overcast day has no sunshine; adjective synonym.

clue.text: Last of sugar in a possible sweet

indicators.note: in places that letter inside the other word

parts.note: doable means possible

indicators.note: last of picks the final letter of the word

explanation.surface: A recipe note: finish adding sugar and a sweet might be possible.
explanation.definitionFit: Sweet in the sense of cute or charming, lovely; an adjective synonym.

clue.text: Discussed place in church for convert

indicators.note: discussed means talked about, so the word is spoken aloud

parts.note: the altar is the table at the east end of a church

explanation.surface: A religious convert talked about a spot in church.
explanation.definitionFit: To convert something is to change or modify it; verb synonyms.

clue.text: Nick parties, going regularly

indicators.note: going regularly asks for every other letter, starting with the first

explanation.surface: A man called Nick goes to parties often.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nick' looks like a name; it is British slang for a jail.
explanation.definitionFit: In British slang a nick is a police station or jail, where offenders are locked up.

clue.text: Sprinter's beginning to catch dawdler

indicators.note: beginning points to the first letter of the word

parts.note: to nail someone is to catch them

explanation.surface: A fast runner starts off in pursuit of a slowcoach.
explanation.definitionFit: The garden mollusc is proverbially slow, so someone who dawdles is likened to one.

clue.text: Attack creatures of the night from below

indicators.note: in a down entry, reading from below means the word runs upwards

parts.note: bats are nocturnal animals

explanation.surface: Night creatures strike up from underneath.
explanation.definitionFit: A stab is a thrust with a knife, a kind of assault; also an attempt.

clue.text: Text without padding encapsulating insignificant message

indicators.note: encapsulating means holding the other piece inside
without padding means the inner filling is removed, leaving only the outside letters

parts.note: wee means tiny or insignificant

explanation.surface: Write a short text with no waffle, wrapping up a trivial message.
explanation.definitionFit: A post on the social platform once called Twitter is a short online message.

clue.text: One of the first leaves piglet ate, poisonous

indicators.note: poisonous food makes the eater go wrong, so the letters are mixed up

explanation.surface: A young pig ate some leaves that turned out to be toxic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leaves' suggests foliage a piglet eats; it means the pages of a book.
explanation.definitionFit: The page bearing a book's name appears near the start, so it is among the first pages.

clue.text: Flies daring to tuck into cabbage and broccoli etc

indicators.note: to tuck into places the daring word inside the vegetables

parts.note: leafy green vegetables are collectively greens
bottle is British slang for nerve or daring

explanation.surface: Flies boldly start eating the vegetables.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tuck into' suggests eating, but it means go inside.
explanation.definitionFit: These are metallic green blowflies, an example of the flies that lay eggs on carrion.
